c1.note: Becker's Oct 27, 2026 article reports Humana confirmed eliminating some jobs while introducing other roles; WHAS11 and WDRB corroborate.

c3.note: The statement wording is quoted by Becker's excerpt and WHAS11 (meet needs of business, greater value for members and patients).

c4.note: WDRB reports Humana wouldn't say how many workers were impacted or which departments; the timeline claim is not explicitly shown, but nondisclosure is consistent.

c8.note: Humana statement: some roles eliminated while new roles created in areas supporting future direction (WHAS11 says 'may be eliminated').

c11.note: WDRB identifies Mark Taylor as director of corporate communications.

c12.note: Taylor's statement says Humana continues to maintain a large employee base in Louisville.

c14.note: WDRB headline and text, published Oct. 26, 2026, report Humana cutting jobs in Louisville as part of a companywide reorganization.

c15.note: WDRB cites Louisville Business First: at least one LinkedIn post said copywriter and content creator roles were eliminated.

c16.note: WDRB states the reorganization followed several changes to executive leadership in recent months.

c17.note: Becker's says the company confirmed the job eliminations in a statement on Oct. 27; no standalone release is evident.

c18.note: Humana would not say how many were affected or which departments; roles are eliminated while others are created, with no stated percentage.

c19.note: WDRB attributes the quote to a statement to Louisville Business First; the claim that no release or filing was found is a negative that can't be fully confirmed, though Becker's and WHAS11 also got statements.

c20.note: Becker's Payer did cover the cuts on Oct. 27; the Kentucky WARN part is unsupported by the passages, but the claim is flagged as unverified.

c21.note: Tracker holds six all-time filings, none since the start of 2025 or in 2026.

c23.note: The Layoff Club summarizes the July/Aug 2026 call: more finance and HR outsourcing, utilization management centralized from 11 markets, and no role counts.

c24.note: The 10-Q reports $179M in charges for the nine months ended Sept. 30, 2026.

c25.note: The 10-Q says the charges primarily relate to severance and associate exit costs, asset impairments and external consulting; the earnings-release wording in variant E is not directly shown, but the substance matches.

c26.note: The 10-Q says 'We expect to incur additional charges over the course of the program.'

c27.note: The charges include impairments and consulting as well as severance, so they are not a headcount figure.

c28.note: The Nov 6 disclosures give charges but no new layoff round or headcount.

c29.note: The 10-K says $329M in severance and employee-related charges for workforce optimization in 2025.

c30.note: The 10-K says $25M in 2024 and $199M in 2023 (both variants correct).

c31.note: 10-K states $199M severance and employee-related charges for workforce optimization in 2023 (and $25M in 2024), so all variants are correct.

c32.note: The 10-K gives the $329M as a dollar charge for severance and other employee-related costs, with no headcount, and it is an aggregate across the year.

c33.note: Humana confirmed some roles may be eliminated as new ones are created, and no numbered mass layoff has been announced; no passage contradicts this.

c34.note: The Q2 2025 call dated July 30, 2025 describes an early retirement program, and the tracker summary matches the quote.

c35.note: The Q2 2025 call takeaways cite expanded outsourcing of shared services, and the tracker says he would contract out more shared services functions.

c36.note: WAVE, published July 29, 2025, reports a voluntary early retirement program for employees in some areas who meet specific requirements.

c37.note: The tracker cites approximately 65,680 for the 2024 10-K and 67,060 for the 2025 10-K, and headcount rose.

c38.note: Crain's reported 1,005 layoffs at the SeniorBridge closure in December 2022, and the tracker says no other round since 2022 carries a count.

c39.note: The Feb 17, 2010 press release confirms the 1,400 net, 2,500 gross and 1,100 added; "last large numbered cut" is an unverified superlative, though the SeniorBridge count conflicts mildly.

c40.note: The saved pages show Humana's cuts mostly as early retirement offers, outsourcing and no WARN filings since 2025.
